title: MnII/III and CeIII/IV Units Supported on an Octahedral Molecular Nanoparticle of CeO2

synthesis.procedure: Under aerobic conditions, benzoic acid was dissolved in diphenyl ether with stirring at 80 °C. Manganese(II) benzoate dihydrate and cerium(III) nitrate hexahydrate were added, followed by portionwise addition of tetrabutylammonium permanganate during a further 5 min of stirring at 80 °C. The solution was heated at 150 °C for 24 h and slowly cooled to ambient temperature over 4 days. After precipitation, the mixture was filtered. The filtrate was layered with nitromethane for 3 days; the resulting microcrystals were filtered, washed with diethyl ether, redissolved in dichloromethane, and layered with nitromethane. Red plate-like crystals of 1·x(solv) grew over 5 days.

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: A central Ce6 octahedron contains a μ6-oxo ion. Its faces connect to an outer layer of twelve MnIII ions arranged as four V-shaped Mn3 units.

synthesis.procedure: Compound 2 was obtained from the precipitate formed in the explicitly quantified preparation of 1. That preparation combined benzoic acid, manganese(II) benzoate dihydrate, cerium(III) nitrate hexahydrate, and tetrabutylammonium permanganate in diphenyl ether, heated the mixture at 150 °C for 24 h, and cooled it over 4 days. The precipitate was dissolved in chloroform and filtered. Layering the filtrate with acetonitrile yielded dark-brown block-like crystals of 2·4CHCl3 over 4 days; these were filtered, washed with cold diethyl ether, and dried under vacuum.

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: Two edge-fused Ce6 octahedra form a Ce10 bioctahedral core. Fourteen surrounding Mn ions form two Mn7 units on opposite sides, giving a Mn7–Ce10–Mn7 sandwich-like arrangement.

synthesis.procedure: Under aerobic conditions, 4-tert-butylbenzoic acid was dissolved in diphenyl ether, followed by manganese(II) nitrate tetrahydrate and cerium(III) nitrate hexahydrate. Tetrabutylammonium permanganate was added slowly in portions during stirring at 80 °C. After another hour at 80 °C, the solution was heated in an oven at 150 °C for 24 h and slowly cooled over 4 days. The solution was kept near 40 °C while filtered, and the filtrate was layered with acetonitrile. Deep-red tetragonal crystals of 3·x(solv) formed within a week; they were filtered, washed with cold acetonitrile, and dried under vacuum.
synthesis.temperature: 80 °C during stirring; 150 °C for reaction; approximately 40 °C during filtration
synthesis.time: 5 min during permanganate addition, then 1 h at 80 °C; 24 h at 150 °C; 4 days cooling; approximately 1 week crystallization
synthesis.vessel_or_method: Stirring followed by heating in a programmable oven; acetonitrile layering
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Filter the cooled solution while near 40 °C; layer the filtrate with acetonitrile, then filter, wash with cold acetonitrile, and vacuum-dry the crystals.

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: A Ce19O32 octahedron with the fluorite arrangement forms the central core. Four additional Ce ions and four Mn5 units attach at its surface and form concentric tetrahedral arrangements around it, yielding the Ce23Mn20 cluster cation.
